speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) whether there are any manpower training programmes tailored for local micro businesses with less than six employees, such as minimarts, to create real business value to the business owners that offset their increased manpower costs incurred by the Progressive Wage Model (PWM); and (b) whether the Ministry will consider targeted PWM exemptions or adjustments for these micro businesses to help alleviate their business costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Each PWM role comes with a list of training modules endorsed by the sectoral Tripartite Cluster.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Besides training their workers, businesses can redesign jobs and transform their business models to improve productivity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: For example, they can tap on the National Trades Union Congress' (NTUC's) Company Training Committee (CTC) Grant, which supports businesses by co-funding their transformation projects to raise productivity, to redesign jobs and to improve work prospects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: This helps businesses cope with the impact of improving the wage outcomes of our lower-wage workers over a five-year period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Beyond improving wage outcomes, we must also ensure that our lower-wage workers continue to be productive in their respective sectors and have meaningful employment through upskilling under PWM.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Businesses must also transform and become more productive, such as through better technology and processes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Employers can tap on the Government measures mentioned to support their business transformation, upskill their workers and defray wage increases.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: And while I am appreciative of PWCS, will MOM consider extending micro businesses with a longer timeline of credit subsidies so that they can have a better chance of transforming their businesses into something that is more relevant for the current economy?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Having said that, I do understand that not every hawker or retailer may understand the schemes.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But rest assured that if they wish to, the SME Centres can support them, if they request such assistance.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, we do have schemes to support, including even the hiring of seniors, for example, because we know many of them are also in some of these micro businesses.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Rest assured that help is at hand and overall, the Government provides the PWCS.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We understand that with the increase in salary or wages that we hope and want to be an outcome of PWMs, that employers are supported, costs are defrayed.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Certainly, this is one way in which the Government, too, wants to support our lower-wage workers through businesses, by giving them meaningful employment.
